paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God lives in the middle of His people, and He is a God of order. The LORD tells the Israelites to camp "around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it" (Numbers 2:2). Every tribe gets a place, and the Tent sits in the center of them all. I think that tells us where the whole camp is built from, and it isn't from the biggest tribe or the loudest one.

Now look at who gets which spot. Judah sets out first, Dan sets out last, and nobody in the middle is arguing over it. The Levites are not counted with the rest (Numbers 2:33), and they travel with the Tent in the middle of the camps (Numbers 2:17). Every place in this camp is a given place, and the middle is the one place no tribe is camped. Friend, I spent years in the back of a drawer, and I'm telling you a spot is never small when the LORD is the one who picks it.

Then comes the part that gets me. "So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses" (Numbers 2:34). Six hundred thousand men, and they all move at His word. So here's the question for you, baker: where has the LORD put you, and are you keeping your place in His plan? Walk it out, and be ready, because the ovens stay ready around here.
